claim: Schmidtea mediterranea is a model organism capable of regenerating any and all of its adult tissues.
source: Schmidtea mediterranea, a model organism capable of regenerating any and all of its adult tissues.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the regenerative capabilities of the model organism.

claim: Microbiome characterization revealed a high Bacteroidetes to Proteobacteria ratio in healthy animals.
source: Microbiome characterization revealed a high Bacteroidetes to Proteobacteria ratio in healthy animals.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract reporting a finding from microbiome characterization.

claim: Perturbations eliciting an expansion of Proteobacteria coincided with ectopic lesions and tissue degeneration.
source: Perturbations eliciting an expansion of Proteobacteria coincided with ectopic lesions and tissue degeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing an observed correlation between bacterial expansion and pathology.

claim: The culture of these bacteria yielded a strain of Pseudomonas capable of inducing progressive tissue degeneration.
source: The culture of these bacteria yielded a strain of Pseudomonas capable of inducing progressive tissue degeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing an experimental result.

claim: RNAi screening uncovered a TAK1 innate immune signaling module underlying compromised tissue homeostasis and regeneration during infection.
source: RNAi screening uncovered a TAK1 innate immune signaling module underlying compromised tissue homeostasis and regeneration during infection.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing a finding from RNAi screening.

claim: TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling mediated opposing regulation of apoptosis during infection versus normal tissue regeneration.
source: TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling mediated opposing regulation of apoptosis during infection versus normal tissue regeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing a finding about the dual role of a signaling pathway.

claim: Microbial dysbiosis underlies persistent inflammatory disorders, chronic non-healing wounds, and scar formation.
source: Microbial dysbiosis, for example, underlies persistent inflammatory disorders, chronic non-healing wounds, and scar formation (Dowd et al., 2008; Price et al., 2009; Carvalho et al., 2012; Scales and Huffnagle, 2013; Brothers et al., 2015; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Long-term management of inflammatory conditions constitutes a substantial and sharply rising burden on our healthcare system.
source: Long-term management of these conditions constitutes a substantial and sharply rising burden on our healthcare system (Sen et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The immune response can play a central role in either promoting or hindering wound healing and tissue regeneration.
source: Significant evidence spanning a diverse array of organisms and tissues indicates that the immune response can play a central role in either promoting or hindering wound healing and tissue regeneration (Eming et al., 2009; Karin and Clevers, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Planaria are a classic model system for studying adult wound healing and tissue regeneration.
source: Planaria are a classic model system for studying adult wound healing and tissue regeneration (Reddien et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Planaria contain a persistent pool of adult pluripotent stem cells, termed neoblasts, capable of regenerating all of the tissues and cell types of the organism.
source: These free living members of the phylum Platyhelminthes contain a persistent pool of adult pluripotent stem cells, termed neoblasts, capable of regenerating all of the tissues and cell types of the organism (Wagner et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Ablation of neoblasts via irradiation eliminates regenerative capabilities, resulting in regression of anterior structures and eventual tissue lysis.
source: Ablation of this population of mitotic cells via irradiation eliminates regenerative capabilities, resulting in regression of anterior structures and eventual tissue lysis (Reddien et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Development of RNAi methodologies has enabled the interrogation of genes involved regeneration.
source: Development of RNAi methodologies has enabled the interrogation of genes involved regeneration (Sanchez Alvarado and Newmark, 1999; Reddien et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Planaria have conserved multiple immune signaling genes.
source: The exemplary regenerative capabilities and conservation of multiple immune signaling genes in planarians make this organism an attractive model for understanding how robust tissue regeneration capabilities can be balanced with an effective immune response (Peiris et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Previous studies in planaria have uncovered components of the immune system conserved in humans, but absent from the well-studied innate immunity models of ecdysozoa.
source: Previous studies in planaria have uncovered components of the immune system conserved in humans, but absent from the well-studied innate immunity models of ecdysozoa (e.g., flies and nematodes) (Abnave et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Planaria reared using traditional static culture methods can exhibit features of declining health including decreased appetite, loss of motility, dorsal tissue lesions, tissue degeneration, and lysis.
source: Planaria reared using traditional static culture methods can exhibit features of declining health including decreased appetite, loss of motility, dorsal tissue lesions, tissue degeneration, and lysis.
evidence: This is a direct observation reported in the introduction.

claim: Many symptoms of declining health in planaria can be temporarily alleviated and managed with antibiotics.
source: Many of these symptoms can be temporarily alleviated and managed with antibiotics, suggesting that endogenous bacteria can play an antagonistic role in normal regenerative and tissue homeostatic functions.
evidence: This is a direct observation reported in the introduction.

claim: Endogenous bacteria can play an antagonistic role in normal regenerative and tissue homeostatic functions in planaria.
source: Many of these symptoms can be temporarily alleviated and managed with antibiotics, suggesting that endogenous bacteria can play an antagonistic role in normal regenerative and tissue homeostatic functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that antibiotics alleviate symptoms.

claim: The composition of the planarian microbiome is still unresolved.
source: Importantly, the composition of the planarian microbiome is still unresolved and no direct link between microbiota, the immune system, and tissue regeneration has been established.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge at the time of the study.

claim: No direct link between microbiota, the immune system, and tissue regeneration has been established in planaria prior to this study.
source: Importantly, the composition of the planarian microbiome is still unresolved and no direct link between microbiota, the immune system, and tissue regeneration has been established.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge at the time of the study.

claim: A novel recirculation culture system was developed for co-cultivation of massive numbers of worms.
source: To increase the scale and efficiency planarian husbandry, we developed a novel recirculation culture system for co-cultivation of massive numbers of worms.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing a methodological development.

claim: The recirculation culture system enables the constant recirculation and UV sanitization of planarian water to mitigate pathogenic levels of bacteria.
source: In brief, this system enables the constant recirculation and UV sanitization of planarian water to mitigate pathogenic levels of bacteria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the function of the recirculation system, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The recirculation culture system results in a permissive context for rearing large biomass levels of healthy, fissioning, lesion-free planarians.
source: The result is a permissive context for rearing large biomass levels of healthy, fissioning, lesion-free planarians.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the outcome of using the recirculation system.

claim: Bacteria tightly associated with the physiology of healthy worms would be preserved within the recirculation culture while additional, potentially harmful species may accumulate upon exit to traditional static culture conditions.
source: We hypothesized that bacteria tightly associated with the physiology of healthy worms would be preserved within this recirculation culture while additional, potentially harmful species may accumulate upon exit to traditional static culture conditions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated by the authors.

claim: The most prevalent bacterial phyla within planaria cultured in the recirculation system was Bacteroidetes.
source: The most prevalent bacterial phyla within planaria cultured in the recirculation system was Bacteroidetes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Bacteroidetes represents a diverse array of key symbionts that support homeostatic functions in mammals.
source: This phylum represents a diverse array of key symbionts that support homeostatic functions in mammals (Rakoff-Nahoum et al., 2004; Mazmanian et al., 2005, 2008; Alegado et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bacteroidetes comprised 78% of the bacterial phyla of planaria from the recirculation system (static culture day 0), but this proportion declined to 57% after 3 days of static culture.
source: Bacteroidetes comprised 78% of the bacterial phyla of planaria from the recirculation system (static culture day 0), but this proportion declined to 57% after 3 days of static culture (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Administration of gentamycin reduced Bacteroidetes composition to 17%.
source: Administration of gentamycin exacerbated this effect, reducing Bacteroidetes composition to 17%.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing.

claim: The proportion of bacteria of the phylum Proteobacteria steadily increased from 9% to 40–44% upon exit from the recirculation system.
source: In the wake of this Bacteroidetes decrease, the proportion of bacteria of the phylum Proteobacteria steadily increased from 9% to 40–44% upon exit from the recirculation system (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Proteobacteria comprises a wide variety of pathogens and increases in its abundance are a hallmark of microbial dysbiosis and pathological inflammation.
source: This phylum comprises a wide variety of pathogens and increases in its abundance are a hallmark of microbial dysbiosis and pathological inflammation (Carvalho et al., 2012; Clark et al., 2015; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Transitions in culture conditions are coincident with shifts in bacterial composition with potential implications for planarian health.
source: Thus, transitions in culture conditions are coincident with shifts in bacterial composition with potential implications for planarian health.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial composition changes.

claim: The most abundant bacterial genera present in recirculation-cultured worms largely belonged to the phylum Bacteroidetes (Candidatus Amoebophilus, Segetibacter, and Chitinophaga) and declined in relative abundance in static culture.
source: The most abundant bacterial genera present in recirculation-cultured worms largely belonged to the phylum Bacteroidetes (Candidatus Amoebophilus, Segetibacter, and Chitinophaga) and declined in relative abundance in static culture (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The genera Oxalobacter, Rhodoferax, and Vogesella, belonging to the phylum Proteobacteria, exhibited proportional increases ranging from 6 to 200 fold in worms transferred to static culture.
source: The genera Oxalobacter, Rhodoferax, and Vogesella, belonging to the phylum Proteobacteria, exhibited proportional increases ranging from 6 to 200 fold in worms transferred to static culture (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Two genera of the phylum Bacteroidetes, Chryseobacterium and Pedobacter, also increased dramatically after transfer despite the net decrease in the phylum overall.
source: Two genera of the phylum Bacteroidetes, Chryseobacterium and Pedobacter, also increased dramatically after transfer despite the net decrease in the phylum overall.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing.

claim: Members of the genus Chryseobacterium are potential pathogens in immune-compromised individuals and newborns undergoing prolonged antibiotic treatment.
source: Members of the genus Chryseobacterium are potential pathogens in immune-compromised individuals and newborns undergoing prolonged antibiotic treatment (Bloch et al., 1997; Calderón et al., 2011), suggesting that dramatic shifts in abundance may constitute an opportunistic infection.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Proportional increases of Pseudomonas in static culture were exacerbated by gentamycin treatment.
source: In contrast, proportional increases of Pseudomonas in static culture were exacerbated by gentamycin treatment (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), consistent with its adept nature to adapt to the selective pressure of antibiotics (Hoffman et al., 2005; Price et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Pseudomonas is adept at adapting to the selective pressure of antibiotics.
source: In contrast, proportional increases of Pseudomonas in static culture were exacerbated by gentamycin treatment (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), consistent with its adept nature to adapt to the selective pressure of antibiotics (Hoffman et al., 2005; Price et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Enrichment of a particular cohort of bacterial species may be more conducive to optimal planarian health and destabilization of this microbiota permits amplification of potentially harmful species.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that enrichment of a particular cohort of bacterial species may be more conducive to optimal planarian health and destabilization of this microbiota permits amplification of potentially harmful species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial composition changes.

claim: Planaria exhibit a robust capacity to replace and integrate missing tissues through a regenerative process combining morphogenesis with the remodeling of pre-existing tissues.
source: Planaria exhibit a robust capacity to replace and integrate missing tissues through a regenerative process combining morphogenesis with the remodeling of pre-existing tissues.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about planarian regeneration.

claim: Three days after amputation, worms exhibited a reciprocal decrease of Bacteroidetes and amplification of Proteobacteria phyla.
source: Three days after amputation, worms exhibited a reciprocal decrease of Bacteroidetes and amplification of Proteobacteria phyla (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing during regeneration, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Un-amputated worms cultured in parallel maintained a relative abundance of Bacteroidetes until the final 2-week time point.
source: In contrast, un-amputated worms cultured in parallel maintained a relative abundance of Bacteroidetes until the final 2-week time point.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing during regeneration.

claim: The genera Candidatus Amoebophilus and Segetibacter, both members of the phylum Bacteroidetes, decreased in abundance 3 days after amputation.
source: The genera Candidatus Amoebophilus and Segetibacter, both members of the phylum Bacteroidetes, decreased in abundance 3 days after amputation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing during regeneration, with reference to Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The genera Acidovorax, Chryseobacterium, Pseudomonas, Vogesella, and Oxalobacter exhibited transient or sustained increases in regenerating worm fragments 3 to 7 days after amputation.
source: In parallel, the genera Acidovorax, Chryseobacterium, Pseudomonas, Vogesella, and Oxalobacter exhibited transient or sustained increases in regenerating worm fragments 3 to 7 days after amputation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing during regeneration, with reference to Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H.

claim: The expansion of Proteobacteria observed in both regeneration and static culture time courses can be traced to common genera amplified under both conditions.
source: Thus, the expansion of Proteobacteria observed in both regeneration and static culture time courses can be traced to common genera amplified under both conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial composition changes.

claim: Phyla composition varied between individual wild planaria.
source: Phyla composition varied between individual animals.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing of wild planaria.

claim: Proteobacteria was either the most abundant (3 out of 5 worms) or the second most abundant (2 out of 5 worms) phyla across all wild worm samples.
source: Proteobacteria was either the most abundant (3 out of 5 worms) or the second most abundant (2 out of 5 worms) phyla across all worm samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing of wild planaria, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The phylum Proteobacteria was proportionally higher in wild collected versus lab-raised worms consistent with observations flies.
source: Furthermore, the phylum Proteobacteria was proportionally higher in wild collected versus lab-raised worms consistent with observations flies (Wong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with a citation to prior research in flies.

claim: The genera that increased during transitions in culture conditions and regeneration, (Chryseobacterium, Vogesella, and Pseudomonas), were detectable in wild planaria samples but present at relatively low levels.
source: Interestingly, we found that the genera that increased during transitions in culture conditions and regeneration, (Chryseobacterium, Vogesella, and Pseudomonas), were detectable in wild planaria samples but present at relatively low levels (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing of wild planaria, with reference to Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1J.

claim: More bacterial genera were common across all four worms collected from site#1 in Sardinia than were unique to any individual.
source: Despite this heterogeneity in bacterial composition, more bacterial genera were common across all four worms collected from site#1 in Sardinia than were unique to any individual (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from 16s rDNA sequencing of wild planaria, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1K.

claim: Greater than 90% of the bacterial genera detected among all of our CIW4 lab strain planaria samples were also detected among our wild worm samples.
source: Furthermore, greater than 90% of the bacterial genera detected among all of our CIW4 lab strain planaria samples were also detected among our wild worm samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 1L).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from 16s rDNA sequencing, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1L.

claim: The vast majority of genera from CIW4 lab strain planaria are common to those of wild type sexual worms.
source: Importantly, our analyses demonstrate that the vast majority of genera from CIW4 lab strain planaria are common to those of wild type sexual worms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial composition overlap.

claim: Removal of animals from the recirculation culture system elicited a 17-fold expansion in 16 s rDNA over three days that was largely mitigated by gentamycin treatment.
source: Removal of animals from the recirculation culture system elicited a 17-fold expansion in 16 s rDNA over three days that was largely mitigated by gentamycin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from qPCR, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1N.

claim: Both removal from the recirculation culture system and amputation elicited a 2- to 3-log fold increase in score-able bacterial species per worm within 3 days.
source: Additionally, both removal from the recirculation culture system and amputation elicited a 2- to 3-log fold increase in score-able bacterial species per worm within 3 days (Figure 1—figure supplement 1O,P).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1O,P.

claim: The observed bacterial bloom was dominated by three bacterial species belonging to the following genera: Vogesella, Chryseobacterium, and Pseudomonas.
source: Representative colony 16 srDNA amplification and sequencing revealed that the observed bacterial bloom was dominated by three bacterial species belonging to the following genera: Vogesella, Chryseobacterium, and Pseudomonas (Figure 2A, Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial colony sequencing, with reference to Figure 2A and Table 2.

claim: The expansion of Vogesella, Chryseobacterium, and Pseudomonas during culture transition was highly reproducible in multiple withdrawals from two independent recirculation culture systems.
source: The expansion of these bacteria during culture transition was highly reproducible in multiple withdrawals from two independent recirculation culture systems (data not shown).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays.

claim: Shifts in microbial composition are coincident with a robust expansion in both absolute bacterial levels and particular bacterial species.
source: Thus, shifts in microbial composition are coincident with a robust expansion in both absolute bacterial levels and particular bacterial species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial composition and levels.

claim: Worms were infected with Vogesella, Chryseobacterium, or Pseudomonas at a concentration of 1E8 CFU/ml.
source: Worms were infected at a concentration of 1E8 CFU/ml and washed every 3–4 days for administration of fresh planaria water containing bacteria.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental method.

claim: This method of infection lead to a dose dependent increase in endogenous bacterial levels over time.
source: This method of infection lead to a dose dependent increase in endogenous bacterial levels over time (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) similar to those observed in the worms following removal from the recirculation system (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Figure 2A.

claim: Feeding of bacteria mixed with beef liver paste elicited an initial spike and steady decline in bacterial levels.
source: In comparison feeding of bacteria mixed with beef liver paste elicited an initial spike and steady decline in bacterial levels as previously reported (Abnave et al., 2014), but the endogenous bacterial levels of control fed worms also increased to match that of bacteria fed worms (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and a citation to prior research.

claim: Infected worms exhibited pathological defects largely resembling planaria of declining health in static culture.
source: In response to infection, worms exhibited pathological defects largely resembling planaria of declining health in static culture (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Infected worms exhibited a consistent development of tissue defects over time varying in the rate of progression by bacterial strain.
source: Infected worms exhibited a consistent development of tissue defects over time varying in the rate of progression by bacterial strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Both the rate of pathological progression and eventual outcome of the infection in planaria varies by bacterial strain.
source: These data demonstrate that both the rate of pathological progression and eventual outcome of the infection in planaria varies by bacterial strain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on pathological progression.

claim: Initially, Pseudomonas mainly localized to the barrier epithelia of the worm in the epidermis and intestine.
source: Initially, Pseudomonas mainly localized to the barrier epithelia of the worm in the epidermis and intestine (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: By 3 days some Pseudomonas appear to have crossed epithelial barriers and localize to the mesenchyme.
source: By 3 days some Pseudomonas appear to have crossed epithelial barriers and localize to the mesenchyme.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining.

claim: Infected worms exhibited a gradual apical compression of the morphology of outer epithelial cells with a slight distortion in the organization of the basement membrane.
source: Infected worms exhibited a gradual apical compression of the morphology of outer epithelial cells with a slight distortion in the organization of the basement membrane.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from histological analysis.

claim: In the intestine, Pseudomonas infection resulted in a pronounced lumenal constriction with changes in epithelial organization and morphology over time.
source: In the intestine, Pseudomonas infection resulted in a pronounced lumenal constriction with changes in epithelial organization and morphology over time.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from histological analysis.

claim: Barrier epithelia represent the initial point of interaction with Pseudomonas.
source: Thus, our data indicate that barrier epithelia represent the initial point of interaction with Pseudomonas and that sustained exposure to this bacterium results in observable cellular and tissue morphology changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial localization.

claim: Sustained exposure to Pseudomonas results in observable cellular and tissue morphology changes.
source: Thus, our data indicate that barrier epithelia represent the initial point of interaction with Pseudomonas and that sustained exposure to this bacterium results in observable cellular and tissue morphology changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on histological changes.

claim: Infected worms exhibited abundant numbers of piwi+ neoblasts both prior to and following tissue degeneration.
source: While infected worms exhibited abundant numbers of piwi+ neoblasts both prior to and following tissue degeneration, the frequency of neoblasts within the interior of the animal relative to the periphery appeared to progressively decrease during infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from WISH analysis, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The frequency of neoblasts within the interior of the animal relative to the periphery appeared to progressively decrease during infection.
source: While infected worms exhibited abundant numbers of piwi+ neoblasts both prior to and following tissue degeneration, the frequency of neoblasts within the interior of the animal relative to the periphery appeared to progressively decrease during infection (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from WISH analysis, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Pseudomonas infection inhibited tissue regeneration of amputated fragments in a dose dependent manner.
source: Pseudomonas infection inhibited tissue regeneration of amputated fragments in a dose dependent manner (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from regeneration assays, with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: Segments of the worm along the A/P axis had different tolerances for bacterial infection.
source: Interestingly, we observed that segments of the worm along the A/P axis had different tolerances for bacterial infection.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from regeneration assays.

claim: Head fragments were the most susceptible to infection, tail fragments exhibited intermediate sensitivity, and trunk fragments were the most resistant.
source: Head fragments were the most susceptible, tail fragments exhibited intermediate sensitivity, and trunk fragments were the most resistant.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from regeneration assays.

claim: Differences in tissue composition along the A/P axis and/or the extent of tissue generation versus remodeling required for re-establishment of the body plan confer resistance or susceptibility to infection.
source: These data suggest that differences in tissue composition along the A/P axis and/or the extent of tissue generation versus remodeling required for re-establishment of the body plan confer resistance or susceptibility to infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on differential susceptibility.

claim: Clustering of the 1,218 genes significantly altered relative to static culture at day 0 revealed transcriptional patterns that were either dependent or independent of antibiotic treatment.
source: Clustering of the 1,218 genes significantly altered relative to static culture at day 0 revealed transcriptional patterns that were either dependent (clusters 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8,and 9) or independent (clusters 3 and 6) of antibiotic treatment (Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from RNAseq analysis, with reference to Figure 3B,C and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Cluster 1 contained two transcripts with homology to peptidoglycan recognition proteins (pgrps), upstream receptors of the IMD pathway in D. melanogaster.
source: Interestingly, this gene cohort contained two transcripts with homology to peptidoglycan recognition proteins (pgrps), upstream receptors of the IMD pathway in D. melanogaster.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from RNAseq analysis.

claim: The IMD pathway represents a conserved branch of the innate immune system with analogous architecture to the inflammatory signaling pathways in vertebrates.
source: Along with Toll signaling, the IMD pathway represents a conserved branch of the innate immune system with analogous architecture to the inflammatory signaling pathways in vertebrates (Panayidou and Apidianakis, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Pseudomonas infection significantly induced pgrp-4.
source: RT/qPCR and WISH analysis confirmed that Pseudomonas infection significantly induced one of these homologous receptors, that we designated pgrp-4 (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from RT/qPCR and WISH analysis, with reference to Figure 3E–G.

claim: Conserved components of the innate immune and inflammatory signaling pathways may dynamically respond to shifts in the microbial composition in planaria.
source: These data suggest that conserved components of the innate immune and inflammatory signaling pathways may dynamically respond to shifts in the microbial composition in planaria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on gene expression changes.

claim: A unidirectional flow system was developed in which worms were maintained in multiple individual containers and steadily flushed with fresh planaria water.
source: To overcome these limitations, we developed a unidirectional flow system in which worms were maintained in multiple individual containers and steadily flushed with fresh planaria water (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing a methodological development, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Culture of planaria under a steady flow rate prevented a 4-log increase in culturable bacteria levels observed in static conditions following exit from the recirculation culture system.
source: Culture of planaria under a steady flow rate prevented a 4-log increase in culturable bacteria levels observed in static conditions following exit from the recirculation culture system (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Introduction of static worms to flow vessels resulted in a nearly 2 log reduction in culturable bacterial levels over 5 days.
source: Additionally, introduction of static worms to flow vessels resulted in a nearly 2 log reduction in culturable bacterial levels over 5 days (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), and worms administered 3 feedings of control dsRNA mixed with beef liver paste maintained levels comparable to those observed in recirculation culture (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The unidirectional flow system provides the necessary conditions to systematically carry out an RNAi screen of infection-modulated genes and to effectively analyze their resulting phenotypes.
source: We conclude from these findings that the unidirectional flow system provides the necessary conditions to systematically carry out an RNAi screen of infection-modulated genes and to effectively analyze their resulting phenotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial levels in the flow system, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A total of 20/35 tested candidate genes resulted in a significant change (2-WAY ANOVA p<0.05) in pathological progression following infection relative to unc controls.
source: A total of 20/35 tested candidate genes resulted in a significant change (2-WAY ANOVA p<0.05) in pathological progression following infection relative to unc controls, while 2/35 genes, bcl2-1 and bcl3-1 aka NFκB-p105, exhibited total lysis prior to infection and were not considered further (Figure 5A) (Pellettieri et al., 2010; Forsthoefel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5A and citations to prior research.

claim: Among the 20 genes that significantly changed pathological progression, 15/20 significantly reduced pathological progression while 5/20 significantly enhanced it.
source: Among these, 15/20 significantly reduced pathological progression while 5/20 significantly enhanced it; we termed these genes activators and inhibitors, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: The homologs of 13/15 activators have been previously shown to be positive regulators of inflammatory or innate immune signaling.
source: Interestingly, the homologs of 13/15 activators (mkk6-1, mkk4, p38-1, pgrp-2, tab1-1, jun D, hep, tak1, jnk, pgrp-3, pgrp-1, xiap, pgrp-1) have been previously shown to be positive regulators of inflammatory or innate immune signaling (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: The homologs for 4/5 inhibitors have been previously shown to inhibit inflammatory and innate immune signaling.
source: Conversely, the homologs for 4/5 inhibitors (pp6, ppm1b, cyld-1, ppm1a) have been previously shown to inhibit inflammatory and innate immune signaling (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: Conserved inflammatory signaling may be largely responsible for mediating tissue degeneration after bacterial infection.
source: Overall the data suggest that conserved inflammatory signaling may be largely responsible for mediating tissue degeneration after bacterial infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on RNAi effects.

claim: RNAi of activators could extend the lesion free period up to 20 days.
source: Control worms remained lesion free for up to 12 days after infection (Figure 5C). RNAi of activators could extend this period up to 20 days.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: RNAi of inhibitors reduced the lesion free period to 6 days.
source: Conversely, RNAi of inhibitors reduced this lesion free period to 6 days.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: RNAi of activators largely delayed the initiation of and the extended the duration of head regression while RNAi of inhibitors expedited and contracted it.
source: With respect to head regression (stage 3), RNAi of activators largely delayed the initiation of and the extended the duration of this stage while RNAi of inhibitors expedited and contracted it (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: Control worms began undergoing lysis by day 12, and 100% of worms lysed 27 days following infection.
source: Following head regression, control worms began undergoing lysis by day 12, and 100% of worms lysed 27 days following infection (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: RNAi of activators delayed and reduced the incidence of lysis and 100% of mkk6-1 and mkk4 RNAi worms survived the entire 30-day duration of the assay.
source: RNAi of activators delayed and reduced the incidence of lysis and 100% of mkk6-1 and mkk4 RNAi worms survived the entire 30-day duration of our assay.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: RNAi of inhibitors induced lysis as early as day 4 with no worms surviving after 9 to 23 days.
source: RNAi of inhibitors induced lysis as early as day 4 with no worms surviving after 9 to 23 days.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: RNAi of many activators increased the incidence, frequency, and duration of head regeneration and subsequent survival during infection.
source: While RNAi of many activators increased the incidence, frequency, and duration of head regeneration and subsequent survival during infection, we observed no incidence of head regeneration following RNAi of the inhibitors pp6, ppm1b, cyld-1 or traf2-1.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: No incidence of head regeneration was observed following RNAi of the inhibitors pp6, ppm1b, cyld-1 or traf2-1.
source: While RNAi of many activators increased the incidence, frequency, and duration of head regeneration and subsequent survival during infection, we observed no incidence of head regeneration following RNAi of the inhibitors pp6, ppm1b, cyld-1 or traf2-1.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen.

claim: mkk4 and mkk6 RNAi worms had the highest incidence of head regeneration while p38-1 RNAi had the lowest despite having a comparable frequency and timing of the initiation of head regression.
source: Amongst activators, mkk4 and mkk6 RNAi worms had the highest incidence of head regeneration while p38-1 RNAi had the lowest despite having a comparable frequency and timing of the initiation of head regression (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: The Phenotype Hierarchy of TAK1 signaling components is largely consistent with the TAK1 signaling pathway in humans.
source: Remarkably, the Phenotype Hierarchy of these components is largely consistent with the TAK1 signaling pathway in humans (Figure 6A,E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from combinatorial RNAi analysis, with reference to Figure 6A,E.

claim: The vast majority of head, trunk, and tail fragments regenerated normally following RNAi of target genes in the absence of infection.
source: The vast majority of head, trunk, and tail fragments regenerated normally following RNAi of target genes in the absence of infection (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from regeneration assays, with reference to Figure 7A,B.

claim: RNAi of the activators largely prevented infection-associated defects in regeneration while RNAi of the inhibitor pp6 exacerbated them.
source: Overall, RNAi of the activators largely prevented infection-associated defects in regeneration while RNAi of the inhibitor pp6 exacerbated them (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from regeneration assays, with reference to Figure 7A,B.

claim: Following infection, 100% of regenerating head fragments in control worms lysed while RNAi of mkk6-1, p38-1, and jnk not only prevented tissue lysis but re-established normal regeneration for 80% of the fragments.
source: Following infection, 100% of regenerating head fragments in control worms lysed while RNAi of mkk6-1, p38-1, and jnk not only prevented tissue lysis but re-established normal regeneration for 80% of the fragments.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from regeneration assays.

claim: RNAi of pp6 exacerbated infection-associated defects resulting in lysis of 100%, 60%, and 100% of regenerating head, trunk, and tail fragments, respectively.
source: Consistent with its role as an inhibitor of TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling, RNAi of pp6 exacerbated infection-associated defects resulting in lysis of 100%, 60%, and 100% of regenerating head, trunk, and tail fragments, respectively (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from regeneration assays, with reference to Figure 7A,B.

claim: Conserved TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling components play a pivotal role in determining regenerative outcomes induced by amputation during infection in a manner consistent with the positional sensitivity of these regenerating fragments along the A/P axis.
source: These results demonstrate that conserved TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling components also play a pivotal role in determining regenerative outcomes induced by amputation during infection in a manner consistent with the positional sensitivity of these regenerating fragments along the A/P axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on regeneration during infection.

claim: WISH analysis of members of the TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling pathway revealed that these components were expressed in largely overlapping patterns of tissues along the planarian body axis.
source: WISH analysis of members of the TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling pathway revealed that these components were expressed in largely overlapping patterns of tissues along the planarian body axis.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from WISH analysis.

claim: The most prominent expression pattern was evident in the planarian gut which was shared in both ordered activators (tak1, jnk, jun D, mkk6-1, and p38-1) and inhibitors (pp6, ppm1b, and cyld-1).
source: The most prominent expression pattern was evident in the planarian gut which was shared in both ordered activators (tak1, jnk, jun D, mkk6-1, and p38-1) and inhibitors (pp6, ppm1b, and cyld-1) (Figure 8A, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from WISH analysis, with reference to Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The human homolog of the kinase p38 is activated via phosphorylation at Thr180 and Tyr182, a region highly conserved in planaria.
source: The human homolog of the kinase p38 is activated via phosphorylation at Thr180 and Tyr182, a region highly conserved in planaria (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A) (Han et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research and reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Both tested phospho-p38 antibodies reacted to an induced band at 45kDa corresponding to the size of planarian p38.
source: UV treatment is a common inducer of P-p38 and western blot analysis revealed both tested antibodies reacted to an induced band at 45kDa corresponding to the size of planarian p38 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from western blot analysis, with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Both polyclonal and monoclonal phospho-p38 antibodies recognized discrete cells above the pharynx.
source: In situ antibody staining revealed that both polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies recognized discrete cells above the pharynx (Figure 8B, Figure 8—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8B and Figure 8—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Treatment with UV irradiation induced a broad antibody staining pattern throughout the gut, mirroring the localized expression of the p38-1 transcript.
source: Treatment with UV irradiation induced a broad antibody staining pattern throughout the gut, mirroring the localized expression of the p38-1 transcript (Figure 8A, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RNAi against planarian p38-1 eliminated the observed P-p38 signal.
source: We tested antibody specificity by determining if RNAi against planarian p38-1 could eliminate the observed signal (Figure 8—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The phospho-p38 antibody specifically recognizes P-p38 in planaria.
source: Thus, we conclude that this antibody specifically recognizes P-p38 in planaria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on antibody specificity.

claim: Prior to Pseudomonas infection, both P-p38+ cells that co-labeled with gut marker mat1 as well as P-p38+mat1- cells adjacent to the gut were observed.
source: Prior to Pseudomonas infection, we observed both P-p38+ cells that co-labeled with gut marker mat1 as well as P-p38+mat1- cells adjacent to the gut (Figure 8B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8B,C.

claim: Six days after infection, large nuclear dense mounds consisting of P-p38+ cells could be observed in the anterior lumen of the gut with more intense lumenal staining also seen in the posterior and regions.
source: Six days after infection, large nuclear dense mounds consisting of P-p38+ cells could be observed in the anterior lumen of the gut with more intense lumenal staining also seen in the posterior and regions (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 2E.

claim: A robust P-p38 staining throughout the interior gut of the head, trunk, and tail fragments was observed within 5 min of amputation overlapping with lumenal nuclear dense mounds.
source: We observed a robust P-p38 staining throughout the interior gut of the head, trunk, and tail fragments within 5 min of amputation overlapping with lumenal nuclear dense mounds (Figure 8D, Figure 8—figure supplement 2F, Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8D, Figure 8—figure supplement 2F, and Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Thirty five to sixty minutes after amputation, signaling coalesced into discrete P-p38+ cells throughout the gut of the resulting fragment.
source: Thirty five to sixty minutes after amputation, signaling coalesced into discrete P-p38+ cells throughout the gut of the resulting fragment (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8D.

claim: P-p38+ cells co-expressed the gut markers mat1 (low), porc, hnf4, and nkx-2.2.
source: Double labeling analysis revealed that these P-p38+ cells co-expressed the gut markers mat1 (low), porc, hnf4, and nkx-2.2 (Gurley et al., 2008; Wagner et al., 2011; Tu et al., 2015) (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from double labeling analysis, with reference to Figure 8E and citations to prior research.

claim: Gut injuries resulting from either lateral incision or needle poke both elicited a similar but more localized P-p38 activation within 30 min.
source: Gut injuries resulting from either lateral incision or needle poke both elicited a similar but more localized P-p38 activation within 30 min (Note: epidermal staining in lateral wound could not be distinguished from background) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2G.

claim: While infection resulted in an increase in P-p38 fraction volume over time, amputation induced a sharp increase in both P-p38 fraction volume and average intensity followed by a gradual decrease.
source: Quantitative image analysis confirmed that while infection resulted in an increase in P-p38 fraction volume over time, amputation induced a sharp increase in both P-p38 fraction volume and average intensity followed by a gradual decrease (Figure 8F,G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from image analysis, with reference to Figure 8F,G.

claim: The downstream kinase of the TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling module is dynamically modulated in response to infection and/or injury within the planarian gut.
source: In either case, our data indicate that the downstream kinase of the TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling module is dynamically modulated in response to infection and/or injury within the planarian gut
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on P-p38 activation.

claim: An anterior/dorsal enriched mesenchymal/epidermal P-p38 staining pattern was induced by Pseudomonas infection.
source: Use of an alternative bleaching solution eliminated background, revealing a previously unresolvable anterior/dorsal enriched mesenchymal/epidermal P-p38 staining pattern that was induced by Pseudomonas infection (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: P-p38+ cells were relatively absent prior to infection but could be visualized in anterior regions within 24 hr of infection and further increased in frequency over the next two days.
source: P-p38+ cells were relatively absent prior to infection but could be visualized in anterior regions within 24 hr of infection and further increased in frequency over the next two days.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining.

claim: Pseudomonas infection induced a similar anteriorly biased induction of apoptosis that coincided with P-p38 activation.
source: We analyzed levels of apoptosis in response to Pseudomonas infection and observed a similar anteriorly biased induction of apoptosis that coincided with P-p38 activation (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from TUNEL analysis, with reference to Figure 9B.

claim: RNAi of pp6 or cyld-1 resulted in elevated numbers of anteriorly biased P-p38+ and TUNEL+ cells both prior to and following Pseudomonas infection.
source: RNAi of either of these genes resulted in elevated numbers of anteriorly biased P-p38+ and TUNEL+ cells both prior to and following Pseudomonas infection (Figure 9C–F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining and TUNEL analysis, with reference to Figure 9C–F.

claim: cyld-1 RNAi resulted in pre-emptive increase in cell proliferation that mirrored the levels observed in control infected worms.
source: Additionally, cyld-1 RNAi resulted in pre-emptive increase in cell proliferation that mirrored the levels observed in control infected worms (Figure 9—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from H3P labeling, with reference to Figure 9—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling plays a role in the control of both a general proliferative response and an apoptotic response during infection.
source: These data support a role for TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling in the control of both a general proliferative response and an apoptotic response during infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on P-p38 activation, apoptosis, and proliferation.

claim: The frequency of P-p38+ cells was consistently lower than that of TUNEL+ cells with only 1–8% overlap depending on RNAi treatment or days post infection.
source: The frequency of P-p38+ cells was consistently lower than that of TUNEL+ cells with only 1–8% overlap depending on RNAi treatment or days post infection (Figure 9E,F, Figure 9—figure supplement 1E, Table 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from image analysis, with reference to Figure 9E,F, Figure 9—figure supplement 1E, and Table 3.

claim: A higher frequency of TUNEL+ cells were proximal to P-p38+ cells (ranging from 12–80%), suggesting a possible extrinsic, rather than an intrinsic role for the mediation of apoptosis.
source: Interestingly, we observed a higher frequency of TUNEL+ cells that were proximal to P-p38+ cells (ranging from 12–80%), suggesting a possible extrinsic, rather than an intrinsic role for the mediation of apoptosis (Figure 9—figure supplement 1F, Table 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a quantitative finding from image analysis, with reference to Figure 9—figure supplement 1F and Table 3, and an inference about the mechanism.

claim: No effects of RNAi of any TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling component on the proliferative burst following amputation were observed.
source: We observed no effects of RNAi of any TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling component on the proliferative burst following amputation (Figure 9—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from H3P labeling, with reference to Figure 9—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Amputation induced apoptosis was increased by RNAi of tak1 or p38-1, and decreased by RNAi of cyld-1.
source: To our surprise, amputation induced apoptosis was increased by RNAi of tak1 or p38-1, and decreased by RNAi of cyld-1 (Figure 9G–J).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from TUNEL analysis, with reference to Figure 9G–J.

claim: This stands in direct contrast to the observed effects of ectopic activation of this pathway in enhancing infection-induced apoptosis.
source: This stands in direct contrast to the observed effects of ectopic activation of this pathway in enhancing infection-induced apoptosis (Figure 9D,F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a comparison between findings, with reference to Figure 9D,F.

claim: tak1 and p38-1 rnai worms all exhibited phenotypically normal regeneration in the absence of infection, suggesting that the observed enhancement in apoptosis is relatively innocuous during normal regeneration.
source: Interestingly, tak1 and p38-1 rnai worms all exhibited phenotypically normal regeneration in the absence of infection (Figure 7), suggesting that the observed enhancement in apoptosis is relatively innocuous during normal regeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from regeneration assays, with reference to Figure 7, and an inference about the significance.

claim: TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling has dual contrasting roles in the control of apoptosis during either infection or regeneration.
source: Overall, our data indicate that TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling has dual contrasting roles in the control of apoptosis during either infection or regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on apoptosis during infection and regeneration.

claim: RNAi of the activator jun D significantly increased bacterial load over time.
source: RNAi of the activator jun D significantly increased bacterial load over time while RNAi of p38-1 had no overall significant effects on Pseudomonas levels (Figure 10A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 10A, B.

claim: RNAi of p38-1 had no overall significant effects on Pseudomonas levels.
source: RNAi of the activator jun D significantly increased bacterial load over time while RNAi of p38-1 had no overall significant effects on Pseudomonas levels (Figure 10A, B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 10A, B.

claim: jun D RNAi worms still exhibited a reduction in bacterial levels from day 6 to day 12, suggesting that jun D independent immune responses also mediate bacterial clearance.
source: Importantly, jun D RNAi worms still exhibited a reduction in bacterial levels from day 6 to day 12, suggesting that jun D independent immune responses also mediate bacterial clearance (Abnave et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with an inference about the mechanism and a citation to prior research.

claim: The planarian immune response is normally coordinated with but not the result of induced apoptosis and tissue degeneration.
source: These data suggest that the planarian immune response is normally coordinated with but not the result of induced apoptosis and tissue degeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial clearance and tissue degeneration.

claim: RNAi of p38-1 results in an identical reduction of bacterial levels in the absence of phenotypic tissue degeneration.
source: While control RNAi worms exhibit the largest decrease in Pseudomonas levels following phenotypic tissue degeneration (Figure 10A–E), RNAi of p38-1 results in an identical reduction of bacterial levels in the absence of phenotypic tissue degeneration (Figure 10B,E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 10B,E.

claim: pp6 and cyld-1 RNAi enhanced tissue degeneration but not bacterial clearance.
source: Similarly, pp6 and cyld-1 RNAi enhanced tissue degeneration but not bacterial clearance (Figure 10C–E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from bacterial CFU assays, with reference to Figure 10C–E.

claim: Pseudomonas infection induces a jun D and p38-1 dependent tissue degeneration response in conjunction with a jun D dependent, p38-1 independent immune response.
source: Thus, Pseudomonas infection induces a jun D and p38-1 dependent tissue degeneration response in conjunction with a jun D dependent, p38-1 independent immune response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial clearance and tissue degeneration.

claim: This study utilized a combination of novel culture methods, bacterial 16 s rDNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling, RNAi screening, and in situ phospho-signaling visualization to illustrate how microbial dysbiosis results in the amplification of pathobionts, compromising tissue homeostasis and regeneration potential via the activation of TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling.
source: In this study, we have utilized a combination of novel culture methods, bacterial 16 s rDNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling, RNAi screening, and in situ phospho-signaling visualization to illustrate how microbial dysbiosis results in the amplification of pathobionts, compromising tissue homeostasis and regeneration potential via the activation of TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's approach and findings.

claim: The ratio of Bacteroidetes to Proteobacteria within the planaria from the recirculation culture system mirrors the distribution of these phyla within the human lower intestinal tract.
source: The ratio of Bacteroidetes to Proteobacteria within the planaria from the recirculation culture system mirrors the distribution of these phyla within the human lower intestinal tract (Human Microbiome Project Consortium, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: This phyla composition is not observed in other invertebrate (e.g., C. elegans and D. melanogaster) or even vertebrate (e.g., D. rerio) model systems that are amenable to large scale genetic screens and have played a pivotal role in shaping our understanding of immunity and host-microbe interactions.
source: This phyla composition is not observed in other invertebrate (e.g., C. elegans and D. melanogaster) or even vertebrate (e.g., D. rerio) model systems that are amenable to large scale genetic screens and have played a pivotal role in shaping our understanding of immunity and host-microbe interactions (Apidianakis and Rahme, 2011; Roeselers et al., 2011; Novoa and Figueras, 2012; Lee and Brey, 2013; Wong et al., 2013; Ermolaeva and Schumacher, 2014; Berg et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: An enrichment in Bacteroidetes in S. mediterranea is significant, as this phylum represents a diverse array of key symbionts known to support proper tissue homeostasis, the development of the immune system, as well as the prevention of inflammatory diseases in mammals.
source: An enrichment in Bacteroidetes in S. mediterranea is significant, as this phylum represents a diverse array of key symbionts known to support proper tissue homeostasis, the development of the immune system, as well as the prevention of inflammatory diseases in mammals, and, intriguingly, have even been linked to the early evolution of multicellular organisms (Rakoff-Nahoum et al., 2004; Mazmanian et al., 2005, 2008; Alegado et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Changes in culture conditions or tissue transection results in an expansion in Proteobacteria, a phenomenon linked to a myriad of human inflammatory disorders.
source: Furthermore, changes in culture conditions or tissue transection results in an expansion in Proteobacteria, a phenomenon linked to a myriad of human inflammatory disorders (Frank et al., 2007; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The ability to induce shifts in the microbiota of wild type animals, uniquely positions planaria as a model for the study of the interrelationship between endogenous bacterial dynamics, tissue homeostasis, and complex tissue regeneration with implications for human health.
source: Our ability to induce shifts in the microbiota of wild type animals, uniquely positions planaria as a model for the study of the interrelationship between endogenous bacterial dynamics, tissue homeostasis, and complex tissue regeneration with implications for human health.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on microbiome dynamics.

claim: Maintenance and care of planarians using traditional static methods can yield variable bacterial levels and composition over time, potentially influencing experimental outcomes.
source: Maintenance and care of planarians using traditional static methods can yield variable bacterial levels and composition over time, potentially influencing experimental outcomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial dynamics.

claim: Prolonged use of antibiotics can lead to the gradual accumulation of resistant pathogenic strains, such as Pseudomonas.
source: Furthermore, prolonged use of antibiotics can lead to the gradual accumulation of resistant pathogenic strains, such as Pseudomonas.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on bacterial dynamics.

claim: Many published phenotypes describing gene knockdowns mirror some of the observed effects of bacterial infection.
source: Given that many published phenotypes describing gene knockdowns mirror some of the observed effects of bacterial infection (Reddien et al., 2005; Forsthoefel et al., 2012; Labbé et al., 2012; Tu et al., 2012), it will be important to examine the extent to which alterations in endogenous bacteria or stimulation of immune signaling underlie these phenotypes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Feeding worms E. coli producing dsRNA elicits robust P-p38 activation.
source: This issue is particularly relevant to the common practice of feeding worms E. coli producing dsRNA as a means of gene function interrogation. As we have demonstrated, this method of RNAi elicits robust P-p38 activation (Figure 8—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from immunostaining, with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 2E.

claim: TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling is multifaceted and can play supportive or antagonistic roles in tissue regeneration.
source: Nevertheless, our study provides further evidence that TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling is multifaceted and can play supportive or antagonistic roles in tissue regeneration (Zarubin and Han, 2005; Cuenda and Rousseau, 2007; Karin and Clevers, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The role of TAK1/MKK/p38 in apoptosis during infection is not unique to planaria.
source: The role of TAK1/MKK/p38 in apoptosis during infection is not unique to planaria.
evidence: This is a statement about the conservation of the mechanism.

claim: In C. elegans, oral Pseudomonas infection initiates programmed cell death of gonadal cells in a p38-dependent manner.
source: In C. elegans, oral Pseudomonas infection initiates programmed cell death of gonadal cells in a p38-dependent manner (Aballay and Ausubel, 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In Drosophila, oral infection induces p38-mediated production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), damaging gut epithelia, and triggering intestinal stem cell activation.
source: In Drosophila, oral infection induces p38-mediated production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), damaging gut epithelia, and triggering intestinal stem cell activation (Buchon et al., 2009; Ha et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Attenuation of TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling in nematodes and flies largely compromises host survival to infection, but substantially enhances host survival in planaria.
source: Interestingly, attenuation of TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling in nematodes and flies largely compromises host survival to infection, but substantially enhances host survival in planaria (Figure 5) (Kim et al., 2002; Buchon et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5 and citations to prior research.

claim: The persistence of a population of adult pluripotent stem cells capable of regenerating all missing tissues uniquely endows planaria with a resilience to somatic tissue damage.
source: One explanation is that the persistence of a population of adult pluripotent stem cells capable of regenerating all missing tissues uniquely endows planaria with a resilience to somatic tissue damage.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Planaria may utilize TAK1 innate immune signaling for a coordinate mounting of antibacterial responses while actively clearing infected tissue via apoptosis prior to the initiation of regeneration.
source: Planaria may utilize TAK1 innate immune signaling for a coordinate mounting of antibacterial responses while actively clearing infected tissue via apoptosis prior to the initiation of regeneration.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The management and care of chronic non-healing wounds poses a substantial and sharply rising burden to our healthcare system and economy.
source: The management and care of chronic non-healing wounds poses a substantial and sharply rising burden to our healthcare system and economy (Sen et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Planaria are capable of resolving tissue degenerative wounds induced by sustained Pseudomonas infection and regenerating lost anterior structures.
source: Of interest is the observation that planaria are capable of resolving tissue degenerative wounds induced by sustained Pseudomonas infection and regenerating lost anterior structures (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation, with reference to Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Antibiotic resistant Pseudomonas is increasing in prevalence in chronic wounds and poses an impediment to effective healing.
source: Antibiotic resistant Pseudomonas is increasing in prevalence in chronic wounds and poses an impediment to effective healing (Dowd et al., 2008; Fazli et al., 2009; Price et al., 2009; Goldufsky et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Results from the RNAi screen have indicated that mkk4 and mkk6-1 may play a role in inhibiting post-infection regeneration in a p38-1 independent manner.
source: Results from our RNAi screen have already indicated that mkk4 and mkk6-1 may play a role in inhibiting this post-infection regeneration in a p38-1 independent manner (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the RNAi screen, with reference to Figure 5F.

claim: Some species of Pseudomonas are capable of attenuating host immune response via secretion of a tyrosine phosphatase that inhibits signaling.
source: In plants, some species of Pseudomonas are capable of attenuating host immune response via secretion of a tyrosine phosphatase that inhibits signaling (Macho et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: S. mediterranea provides a basis for dissecting the duality of evolutionarily conserved inflammatory signaling in complex, multi-organ adult tissue regeneration.
source: Given the complex role of inflammation in either the hindrance or support of reparative wound healing and regeneration, S. mediterranea provides a basis for dissecting the duality of this evolutionarily conserved inflammatory signaling module in complex, multi-organ adult tissue regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on TAK1/MKK/p38 signaling.

claim: The conservation of bacterial phyla composition and dynamics uncovered in this invertebrate make it the first non-murine model organism for the study of pathological shifts in endogenous bacteria with relevance to human disease.
source: Furthermore, the conservation of bacterial phyla composition and dynamics we uncovered in this invertebrate make it the first non-murine model organism for the study of pathological shifts in endogenous bacteria with relevance to human disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed data on microbiome composition.
